allometry.note: Rough heights from general knowledge of the species: about 1.2 m at 15 years and 1.7 m at 40. Wide tolerances.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye from photographs: yellow-green to grey-green fans.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a shrubby palm 1 to 2 m tall whose trunks creep along or under the ground and branch into wide clumps, with stiff fan fronds about 1 m across on toothed petioles, yellow-green to silvery. Not fitted to measurements.

generator.params.dead_angle.note: Dransfield et al. (Genera Palmarum, 2nd ed., 2008), under the genus: it grows in clusters of stems; its dead leaves stay on the stem (marcescent) rather than falling cleanly.

generator.params.dead_life.note: Dransfield et al. (Genera Palmarum, 2nd ed., 2008), under the genus: it grows in clusters of stems; its dead leaves stay on the stem (marcescent) rather than falling cleanly.

generator.params.leaflet_scatter.note: What the palm program's values mean for a palm's stated characters: its frond is its whole leaf; fan or feather from its division pattern, with the petiole, its girth, rachis pieces and frond angles of the built-in fan or feather palms; suckers if it is clonal; the trunk's rise from its usual height less the crown, and its girth from its stated diameter or else its height.

generator.params.skirt.note: Dransfield et al. (Genera Palmarum, 2nd ed., 2008), under the genus: it grows in clusters of stems; its dead leaves stay on the stem (marcescent) rather than falling cleanly.

generator.program.note: The lineage's own program (growth plan G2.3a), on the palm base: it gives the values its species leave unset, which the palm program gave as defaults until then.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy (plant forms milestone F4). Calibration against measurements and photographs comes later.
